items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We were engaged to do a recording for a producer named Alan Bates which was for the 27th of April.

ctx.x: After three rehearsals at a club called Tally-Ho, the first concert took place the 21st of April at the Rugby Football club in Osterley where the first one with Bruce Turner had been played. The sextet was known as a semi-professional orchestra because Tony and Alan had another profession and did not depend on music as a living. But they played better than some professionals that I had come across in my travels and the group as a whole were real tight and could swing like mad.

The next stop was Birmingham again, then Manchester and Morden. Buck Clayton was in London during this time and Ben Webster was playing at Ronnie Scott's club. We were engaged to do a recording for a producer named Alan Bates which was for the 27th of April.

I arrived at the studio that morning and learned that Buck had been taken to a hospital the night before, suffering from a nose haemorrhage. The rhythm section was from the Alex Welsch orchestra and Jack Higgins was in charge of the date.
